Special education teachers adapt curricula and materials to students' educational needs, deliver individual, small-group or class instruction, record progress and collaborate with parents, general education teachers and support teams. This page covers multiple stages from preschool to secondary school; the US statistics use the 25-2050 occupational family and do not treat an elementary sub-occupation profile as all teachers.
Overall page: BLS25-2050 special education teacher family; Chinese professional standards cover different stages and educational institutions.

entries: Educational needs｜Determine teaching needs by combining existing educational assessments and performance.｜Hand over the educational basis; medical diagnoses must not be made from it.
Objectives and plans｜Set observable objectives and adapt curricula, activities and materials.｜Hand over the objectives, support conditions and review arrangements.
Instructional delivery｜Deliver class, small-group or individual instruction according to student needs.｜Real delivery requires training, qualifications and institutional arrangements.
Progress assessment｜Record responses, prompts and observation conditions.｜Distinguish independent performance from assisted completion, and keep the gaps.
Home-school collaboration｜Communicate with parents, general education teachers and support staff.｜State the facts and pending questions, without guaranteeing outcomes.
Stage transitions｜Support transitions between grades or to life outside school.｜Collaborative plans are implemented according to the stage and team authority.

paragraphs:
Setting｜Most work in schools in the United States, some in home or other settings; the Chinese configuration is checked separately.
Stage｜Curriculum and transition tasks vary from preschool age to secondary school, and the overall page does not merge them into a single timetable.
Classroom｜May involve class, small-group or one-to-one teaching; class size is not inferred from this page.
Records｜Lesson preparation, performance records and plan updates are part of teaching.
Collaboration｜Parents, teacher assistants, general education teachers and specialists have different roles.

Hours｜Outside US school hours there may be lesson preparation and meetings; in China this is checked against the contract and the actual arrangements.
Load｜BLS describes possible emotional strain and physical load, and the description is not an incident rate.
Technology｜Recording tools and assistive communication technology do not equal generative AI adoption.
Boundaries｜Teaching qualifications do not automatically grant medical diagnosis or all rehabilitation operating authority.

items.title: What do employers usually look for in recruitment?

values: P1–P4 materials｜All fictional, paper exploration only

You are to check a fictional teaching record and hand over the objective card, material adaptation note, recalculation table and home-school handover. Only the anonymous symbol A is used; it contains no real student identity or diagnosis, no teaching is delivered and no diagnosis is made.

P1: the objective is to point out the circle within 10 seconds of presenting one two-image card and giving the spoken task point out the circle, without extra prompting. Each presentation counts as 1 opportunity. I means correct without extra prompting, P means correct after extra spoken prompting and W means wrong or no response; a blank does not equal I. There are 5 opportunities each time, and the paper achievement condition is at least 4 I in each of 3 consecutive observations under the same material conditions.

P2: the 1st observation uses the M1 two-image card, recording I, P, W, I, blank; the 2nd still uses M1, recording I, I, P, I, W. Both times have 5 presentations, recorded by observer B, and the reason for the blank row is unknown.

P3: the 3rd time uses the M2 enlarged two-image card, recording I, I, I, I, W; still 5 presentations. The 3rd time also changes the material, so these three records cannot be used to assert that M2 caused the progress. Total correct includes I+P, independent correct includes only I, and the denominator is fixed at 5 presentations.

P4: paper suggestions only. Teacher B checks the blank row and objective conditions, team member C reviews the material plan and the subsequent comparable records, and communicator D receives the home-school feedback draft. Without review, do not write objective achieved or implemented next time, and whether M2 will be used next time and the observation arrangements are not yet decided.

It can be handled on paper or in a spreadsheet in 30–45 minutes; mark the output v1 and note P1/P2/P3/P4 for each conclusion. If a conclusion cannot be supported, keep it pending and do not fabricate student responses.
Tasks and output

Hand over the P1 objective card: behaviour, material, task wording, 10 seconds, prompt definitions, the denominator each time and the 3 consecutive conditions. Hand over the P2 material note: what changed from M1 to M2, how other conditions and records are kept consistent, and the plan for team review.

Hand over the P3 observation-by-observation recalculation: how many I, P, W and missing each time, with the independent and total correct proportions calculated separately; write the boundaries of achievement and causal judgment. Hand over P4 neutral feedback and to-dos: missing items, material changes, recipients and undecided matters, without declaring real educational effects.
Reference answer｜Do it independently first, then look

1st time I=2, P=1, W=1, missing=1, independent 2/5=40%, total correct 3/5=60%; 2nd time I=3, P=1, W=1, independent 3/5=60%, total correct 4/5=80%; 3rd time I=4, P=0, W=1, independent 4/5=80%, total correct 4/5=80%. Blanks do not count as correct and the denominator is not reduced to 4.

The condition of at least 4 I under the same material in 3 consecutive observations is not yet met: the first two M1 observations had only 2 and 3 I respectively, and the 3rd M2 had 4 I only once. Mastery, diagnosis or improvement caused by M2 cannot be asserted; the material change and the small number of observations limit comparability. The P2 plan can suggest enlarging the presentation and keeping the task and record definitions, and is passed to the team for review rather than being implemented directly.

P4 example: the independent correct results in the records are 2/5, 3/5 and 4/5, the material was changed to M2 on the 3rd occasion, and one row in the first round is missing, so objective achievement cannot be confirmed from this. Ask B to check the reason for the blank and the conditions, C to check the material and subsequent record arrangements, and D to check the feedback scope and receiving permissions; this is currently a draft only and the follow-up is undecided.
Boundaries and review

All are fictional by the author, and the paper achievement conditions are not a universal teaching standard. Review the objectives, prompts and denominators, the 3 same-material conditions, the missing data and causal limits and the recipients; do not use real student records or provide medical diagnosis, crisis intervention or physical restraint guidance.
